caption: The drawing depicts a lion standing with its right front paw placed on a spherical object that appears to be a ball. The lion's mane is rendered with a detailed texture using a combination of brown, white, and dark sepia tones, creating a dense, curly appearance. The face of the lion is light brown with shading around the eyes, nose, and mouth, showing an open mouth with visible teeth and a curled upper lip. The body of the lion features a combination of earth tones such as tan, green, and brown, with some faint dappling and striping evident along its back and legs. The paws are also highlighted with a similar earthy palette, and the rear legs display blotches of green, blue, and brown hues. The tail loops up along the back, with a lighter coloration, mainly tan with hints of yellow and brown. The ball beneath the right front paw is round and shaded with green, yellow, and brown, giving it a mottled appearance. The background is a plain, untextured off-white, with some faint writing and measurement marks around the edges.
title: Lion and Ball Figurine
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
